label: Step L+1 (re-input of first token) in long sequences starting with t/c/e
explanation: Almost all activation (99%) sits on the copy step right after <DEL> (recall_idx==1), where the input is the fed-back first original token and the model is about to emit original token 1. The feature fires only on long sequences: L=9 holds 63% of mass, L=8 28%, L=7 8%, and L<=6 roughly none. It also fires only for some first tokens: t (53% of mass), c (26%), e (10%), then a little 3/o/z/u/0, and never others such as a or b. Which token is being output (orig(1)) also matters: z/t/e/o/c/w raise the rate, and restricting to those lifts precision to about 0.3-0.5 but costs recall. Even within the best cell (L=9, first token t) only about a third of steps fire, so the feature seems to fire when several of these factors (length, first token, second token) add up past a threshold. The simple conjunction catches about 80% of activation mass but with low precision (~0.08). It does not fire in the original phase, at the delimiter (3 hits), or at later copy steps. Magnitude is roughly flat (0.10-0.22); top activations are mostly first-token t or c with L=9.
